name: The Caledonian Edinburgh
insider_take: This grand Victorian railway hotel has been Edinburgh's most prestigious address since 1903, where royalty and celebrities have made history beneath its iconic clock tower.
whats_special: The Caledonian sits at the west end of Princes Street, directly above the former Princes Street Station. Its famous clock tower has been a Edinburgh landmark for over a century, and the hotel boasts one of the city's most spectacular views of Edinburgh Castle. The building's red sandstone façade is a masterpiece of Edwardian architecture, and it was once the terminus hotel for the Caledonian Railway.
pro_tip: Request a castle-view room on the upper floors for unobstructed panoramas of Edinburgh Castle, especially magical during the Festival Fireworks or Hogmanay celebrations.
dont_miss: The hotel's afternoon tea service and the historic Caley Bar, famous for its whisky collection. Step outside to explore Princes Street Gardens directly across the street, or take the short walk to the Royal Mile and Edinburgh Castle. The hotel's location makes it the perfect base for Edinburgh Festival events.
pros: Iconic Victorian railway hotel with stunning Edinburgh Castle views
Prime location at west end of Princes Street for shopping and attractions
Grand historic architecture with elegant period features and modern luxury
Exceptional service standards befitting a landmark heritage hotel
cons: Premium pricing reflects prestigious location and heritage status
Historic building may have varying room sizes and layouts
